candidates.label: Praise of Allah (Hamd)
candidates.definition: The Qur'anic affirmation that praise belongs to Allah, opening al-Fatiha. Related to but not identical with shukr (gratitude); the precise relationship requires scholarly review.

evidence.rationale: The verse explicitly states that praise is due to Allah; the concept's own terms appear in the text.

existingTopicOverlap.note: Shukr is gratitude for favor; hamd is praise. Classical scholarship distinguishes them; this candidate records hamd as its own Qur'anic concept.

candidates.label: Allah's Lordship of the Worlds (Rabb al-'Alamin)
candidates.definition: Allah's lordship over all worlds as affirmed in 1:2. Records the Qur'anic phrase and its immediate context; theological elaboration belongs to tafsir.

evidence.rationale: The verse names Allah as Rabb of all worlds; the exact phrase is present.

existingTopicOverlap.note: The existing topic covers oneness of lordship; this candidate records the specific Qur'anic affirmation of Allah as Rabb of all worlds. Whether they should merge is a scholarly decision.

candidates.label: The paired divine names ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim
candidates.definition: The paired divine names ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim as they occur together in al-Fatiha (1:1, 1:3). Their pairing and repetition are the extracted phenomenon; interpretation of the distinction belongs to tafsir.

evidence.rationale: Both names appear together in the basmala.
The pair is repeated as a complete verse, marking emphasis within the passage.

existingTopicOverlap.note: These are two of the divine names; the existing topic covers the names collectively.

candidates.label: Sovereignty of the Day of Recompense (Malik Yawm ad-Din)
candidates.definition: Allah's sovereignty of the Day of Recompense as stated in 1:4. Distinct from a general hereafter topic: the extracted concept is Allah's ownership/sovereignty of that Day.

evidence.rationale: The complete verse states the concept explicitly.

existingTopicOverlap.note: The existing topic covers the Day itself; this candidate records the sovereignty aspect affirmed here.

candidates.label: Exclusive worship and seeking help (Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in)
candidates.definition: The declaration that worship and seeking help are directed to Allah alone (1:5). The classical link to tawhid al-uluhiyyah is noted as related but requires tafsir evidence to assert.

evidence.rationale: The complete verse is the declaration itself; both verbs (worship, seek help) are explicit.

existingTopicOverlap.note: Tafsir literature cites this verse for oneness of worship; that identification is recorded as related, not asserted as verified evidence.

candidates.label: The taught supplication for guidance to the straight path
candidates.definition: The supplication the Qur'an teaches believers to make: asking Allah for guidance to the straight path (1:6), specified in 1:7 as the path of the favored.

evidence.rationale: The imperative plea 'guide us' with its object 'the straight path' is the verse itself.
The continuation specifies whose path is meant, completing the taught supplication.

existingTopicOverlap.note: A specific Qur'an-taught supplication within the general supplication topic.

candidates.label: The three groups: favored, anger-earned, astray
candidates.definition: The distinction stated in 1:7 between those upon whom Allah bestowed favor, those who earned anger, and those astray. The verse does not name the groups; any identification requires verified tafsir evidence and is not asserted here.

evidence.rationale: The two negative categories are named explicitly; the favored category appears earlier in the same verse. The three-way distinction is the extracted concept, without identifying the groups.

candidates.notes: No existing curated or scholarly topic records this specific three-way distinction; flagged as a gap candidate. Group identification is deliberately deferred to scholarly review with tafsir evidence.
